output.title: What folder structure usually hides in a small business
output.body:
For a small business owner, messy folders usually hide a simpler problem: repeated document search. If you keep hunting for customer agreements, invoices, contracts, or past decisions, the folder tree is not the real workflow. It is where the friction shows up.

The bounded decision is not “reorganise everything.” It is: should the next automation effort start only after you can name one repeatable document task that matters, such as invoice filing, contract retrieval, or answering a customer query from old files? That is a threshold question, not a full system rebuild.

A practical check is simple: for one week, pick your most common lookup and note three things each time it happens. What were you looking for? Which folders did you check? How long did it take before you found it, or gave up and asked someone else? That is just manual work, but it tells you whether the problem is occasional clutter or a recurring process worth tightening.

If the same lookup keeps showing up and takes real time, you may have a workflow worth automating later. If it is ad hoc or takes seconds, the folder structure may be annoying, but not yet a business process. The folder names are often the smoke, not the fire.
